newsitem.title: USA: NY comptroller rejects Washington's offers - paper.
newsitem.headline: NY comptroller rejects Washington's offers - paper.

text.p: New York State Comptroller H. Carl McCall, a Democrat who is considered a potential challenger to Republican Gov. George Pataki, rejected offers to join the Clinton Administration, the Albany Times Union said Thursday.
The comptroller told the paper that "several weeks ago there were some overtures made. I made it clear I was not interested."
The subject was not raised on Tuesday, when McCall met with Vice President Al Gore in New York City, he added.
The paper added there was speculation by Democratic Party insiders that McCall might be interested in an international spot, like U.S. trade representative or ambassador to the United Nations.
McCall, who is 61, was elected to a four-year term as comptroller in 1994.
